authorship: Luma original guidance and editable path examples, informed by the engineering references below. No upstream code or model weights copied; not a validated art curriculum.

sources.use: Stroke sequences, pen lifts, uniform scaling and simplified line vocabulary. Dataset samples are credited separately in drawing-library.json.
Controlled curvature, preserving endpoints, sparse hachure and repeatable geometry. Adapted as original planning guidance; no Rough.js dependency or copied implementation.

techniques.label: 少笔画表达 / stroke economy
steps: Identify ONE missing local feature; use its silhouette before adding texture. Keep the child's existing outline.
Prefer one continuous Q or C curve over many tiny zigzags; lift the pen between genuinely separate marks. Usually use 1–3 paths.
Retain the child's proportions and brush. Stop with room for their next contribution.
techniques.avoid: Do not redraw the whole subject, impose perfect symmetry or add repeated outlines just to look hand-drawn.

exampleAddition.subject: one simple arch
exampleAddition.requires: Illustrates curve economy only; choose a meaningful local feature and orient it from the actual canvas.

techniques.label: 沿连接点起笔 / connected curve
steps: Locate the actual supporting contour and confirm which body part it belongs to.
Place the first M at the visible junction; let one or two curves grow into available space. Mirror or rotate for the subject's real direction.
Keep that endpoint fixed while sizing the new part. Reuse exactly the same geometry for preview and commit.
techniques.avoid: No floating tail, whisker or stem; do not move a junction onto a different body part to dodge a collision.

exampleAddition.subject: one connected curl
exampleAddition.requires: First M touches supporting ink. The illustrated growth is rightward; choose the actual placement and attachment on the original canvas.

techniques.label: 轮廓内添细节 / inset detail
steps: Find an actually empty interior surface such as an ear, wing, shell or clothing panel.
Add one small arc or oval following that surface's orientation; leave a visible gap from the outer contour.
Keep existing eyes, mouth, strings and markings clear. Omit the detail when the interior is already crowded.
techniques.avoid: Do not add a second outline around the whole subject or put an interior feature outside its supporting surface.

exampleAddition.subject: one small oval detail
exampleAddition.requires: Requires a visible empty interior patch; set placement=inside and position relative to that supporting region.

techniques.label: 稀疏纹理 / sparse texture
steps: Use texture only when the existing subject has a suitable visible surface, such as bark, a mane or a shell.
Choose 2–3 short strokes following the surface direction and leave more blank space than ink.
Keep strokes separated, inside the same surface, and away from important features. Preserve the current brush.
techniques.avoid: No dense hatching, black fill, noisy randomized scribbles or texture across the child's face and outline.

exampleAddition.subject: three sparse surface marks
exampleAddition.requires: Interior surface must be large enough for gaps wider than the current brush; otherwise choose a single detail.

techniques.label: 有间隔的重复线 / spaced repeated lines
steps: Identify a real functional surface, such as a guitar neck or a train panel, and inspect existing lines first.
Use 2–3 separated lines in the same local direction; adapt their length to that surface instead of copying reference coordinates.
Keep the spacing visible at the child's brush width. Fewer readable lines are preferable to an exact but crowded count.
techniques.avoid: Do not cross the supporting contour, duplicate existing strings or turn a tilted object upright.

exampleAddition.subject: three spaced strings
exampleAddition.requires: Requires a visible clear elongated surface. Rotate with it, and connect line ends only where actual supporting ink exists.

techniques.label: 留给孩子的下一笔 / open continuation
steps: Follow a visible endpoint or a clear contour relationship without guessing an object name.
Add one short curve whose starting direction continues the existing gesture; keep the junction on real ink.
Leave a new reachable endpoint and enough empty space for the child to respond. A closed form can support an attached open line.
techniques.avoid: Do not force every unknown shape into an animal, trace the last line, or close and complete the whole drawing.

exampleAddition.subject: one open sweeping line
exampleAddition.requires: Select a real endpoint or meaningful junction; use the child's gesture to choose direction. First M is the connection end.
